statements.t: “Our third quarter results fell short of our expectations, largely due to Argo’s slower than anticipated financial recovery, with incremental pressure from higher input costs and consumer softness,” said Jim Zallie, chairman, president and CEO of Ingredion.
While we expect these actions to improve earnings, the recovery is taking longer than we expected.”

“As a result, we are lowering our full-year outlook, primarily to reflect the slower earnings recovery in Food & Industrial Ingredients—U.S./CAN, along with the impacts of higher input costs and softer demand.”
Through September 30, the Company repurchased $85 million of common stock and is on track to complete its $100 million full-year share repurchase target.
The Company now expects its full-year 2026 reported diluted EPS to be in the range of $8.04 to $8.49, and its adjusted diluted EPS to be in the range of $9.25 to $9.70.

The Company now expects full-year 2026 net sales to be flat, reflecting volume growth and favorable foreign exchange, offset by lower price mix as well as the impact of the previously mentioned sale of its majority stake in the Pakistan business.
For full-year 2026, the Company expects a reported effective tax rate of 27.9% to 28.9% and expects an adjusted effective tax rate of 26.5% to 27.5%.
